text:
Vegas arrives in Detroit on the third stop of a four-game road trip, 1-0-1 so far, after a 3-2 win at Pittsburgh where Tomas Hertl scored the winner with 0:35 left, having trailed in the third. The Golden Knights are 2-1-2 in their last five and are without Parker Wotherspoon. Detroit lost 4-2 at Tampa Bay and is without Dylan Larkin (suspension), Marco Kasper and Mason Appleton. With Larkin out, Alex DeBrincat has moved beside Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson, and Emmitt Finnie has moved onto the first power-play unit.

Our numbers see little between them. Each team has taken 53% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) at five on five, and our model has VGK at 3.0 goals tonight and DET at 2.89. Detroit is better than its record: a -2 goal difference on +5.2 expected, with finishing costing it 7.0 goals. Detroit's power play (0.82 expected goals per game) tops Vegas's (0.73), but its penalty kill allows 0.74 per game to Vegas's 0.46. In net, projected starter Daniil Tarasov is +6.5 goals saved above expected this season, against +0.1 for Carter Hart. Last year the numbers were -2.8 for Tarasov and -4.4 for Hart.

Mitch Marner has a point in 10 straight games and an 11-game streak by our count, 70% to record one tonight. Mark Stone, 35% to score, just picked up goal No. 10, per CBS Sports. For Detroit, DeBrincat and Arvidsson are each 35% to score, and Raymond has points in five straight.
